name: 2 Baruch
sourceNote: This English text was prepared from the public-domain English edition of R. H. Charles, *The Apocalypse of Baruch* (1896, revised in *The Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament*, 1913), which renders the Syriac text of Antonio Ceriani's edition of the Ambrosian manuscript. The wording here is new and not a copy of Charles; his work was used to follow the sense and to keep each verse in his verse division, which most English readers of the book use. Charles's brackets and conjectures are not reproduced. Verses that Charles printed in parallel from the Greek fragment of chapters 12–14 are not given, because they are not part of the Syriac text. The divine name is not written out in the Syriac; God is called "the Mighty One," "the Most High," and "the Lord," and this book keeps those titles. **Date and text.** The story is set in the days of the fall of Jerusalem to the Babylonians in 587/586 BC, but the book was written after the Romans destroyed Jerusalem in AD 70, most likely around AD 100, and it answers the same question as 4 Ezra: why did God let this happen, and what comes next? Most scholars think it was written in Hebrew, translated into Greek, and from Greek into Syriac. The Greek is lost except for one small papyrus fragment from Oxyrhynchus (P.Oxy. 403), which parallels part of chapters 12–14. The whole book survives in one Syriac manuscript of the sixth or seventh century, in Milan. The "Letter of Baruch" (chapters 78–86) also circulated separately and is found in other Syriac Bible manuscripts. An Arabic version of the book was made from the Syriac. **Numbering.** The book has 87 chapters, and the verse counts follow Charles. **Canon status.** 2 Baruch is not in the Jewish Bible, nor in the Catholic, Orthodox, or Protestant canons. Its closing Letter was copied in some Syriac Bible manuscripts. **About the book.** In 2 Baruch, the scribe Baruch, son of Neriah, hears from God that Jerusalem will fall, and he watches angels tear down its walls and hide the temple vessels. He mourns, fasts, and receives visions: a forest, a vine, and a spring that overcome a great cedar, the dark and bright waters of twelve ages of history, and the coming of the Messiah, who judges the nations and begins an age without pain. Baruch learns that the righteous will rise with the same bodies and then be changed to shine like angels, that Adam's sin brought death but each person chooses his own reward, and that the law, not the temple, is what keeps Israel alive. He is told to teach the people for forty days and sends one letter to the exiles in Babylon and another by eagle to the nine and a half tribes beyond the Euphrates. The book was meant to comfort Jews after AD 70 and to urge them to keep the law while they wait for God's end.

verses.text: In the twenty-fifth year of Jeconiah,{a} king of Judah{b}, the word of the Lord came to Baruch{c} son of Neriah.{d} It said to him,
"Do you see everything these people are doing to Me? The wrongs of these two tribes that were left are worse than the wrongs of the ten tribes that were carried off into exile.
The earlier tribes were pushed into sin by their kings, but these two have pushed and pressed their own kings to sin.

So I am bringing disaster on this city. For a time it will be taken out of My sight, and I will scatter this people among the nations so that they may do those nations good. My people will be disciplined, and a time will come when they will long for the good days they once had."

notes.text: "Jeconiah" is another name for King Jehoiachin; the Hebrew form *Yekonyah* means "Yahweh will establish." He was taken to Babylon in 597 BC, and the book dates its opening scene by his reign, though the story itself is set later, at the fall of Jerusalem in 587/586 BC.
"Judah" (Hebrew *Yehudah*) is linked in Genesis 29 with "praise." It names the southern kingdom.
"Baruch" (Hebrew *Barukh*) means "blessed." He is the scribe who wrote down Jeremiah's words in the book of Jeremiah.
"Neriah" (Hebrew *Neriyyah*) means "lamp of Yahweh."

chapters.heading: The coming destruction of Jerusalem announced to Baruch

verses.text: "I have told you this so that you can tell Jeremiah{a} and everyone like you to leave this city.
For your works are like a solid pillar under this city, and your prayers like a strong wall around it."

notes.text: "Jeremiah" (Hebrew *Yirmeyahu*) is traditionally explained as "Yahweh raises up" or "Yahweh loosens."

verses.text: I answered, "O Lord, my Lord, did I come into the world only to watch my mother{a} suffer? No, my Lord!
If I have found favor with You, take my spirit first, so that I may go to my fathers and not see my mother destroyed.
Two things press hard on me: I cannot stand against You, and my soul cannot bear to see my mother suffer.
But let me say one thing before You, Lord.
What will happen after all this? If You destroy Your city and hand over Your land to those who hate us, how will the name of Israel{b} ever be remembered again?

Who will sing Your praises? To whom will the teaching of Your law be explained? Will the world go back to what it was before creation, and the age return to the silence of the beginning? Will the whole multitude of souls be swept away and the human race never be named again? And where is everything You promised about us?"

notes.text: The city of Jerusalem, called here "my mother," as Zion is often pictured as a mother in the Hebrew prophets.
"Israel" (Hebrew *Yisrael*) is explained in Genesis 32 as "he struggles with God."

verses.text: The Lord said to me, "This city will be handed over for a time. The people will be disciplined for a time. But the world will not be given over to oblivion.
Do you think this is the city of which I said, 'I have carved you on the palms of My hands'?

The building that stands among you now is not the one that is kept with Me, the one that was prepared long ago, from the moment I planned to make Paradise, and that I showed to Adam{a} before he sinned. When he disobeyed the command, it was taken from him, just as Paradise was.
Afterward I showed it to My servant Abraham{b}, by night, among the halves of the sacrificed animals.
And again I showed it to Moses{c} on Mount Sinai, when I showed him the pattern of the tent and all its furnishings.
Now it is kept safe with Me, like Paradise.
So go, and do what I have commanded you."

notes.text: "Adam" (Hebrew *adam*) means "human being," from the word for the ground, *adamah*.
"Abraham" (Hebrew *Avraham*) is explained in Genesis 17 as "father of a multitude."
"Moses" (Hebrew *Mosheh*) is linked in Exodus 2 with "drawing out."

chapters.heading: The heavenly Jerusalem

verses.text: I answered, "So I am to grieve over Zion{a}. Your enemies will come to this place and defile Your sanctuary, carry Your inheritance off into captivity, and lord it over those You have loved. Then they will go back to the home of their idols and boast in front of them. What will You do for Your great name?"
The Lord said to me, "My name and My glory last forever, and My judgment will take its own course in its own time.
You will see with your own eyes that the enemy will not overthrow Zion or burn Jerusalem{b}. They will only serve for a while as the Judge's instruments.
But go and do everything I have told you."
So I went and took Jeremiah, Adu,{c} Seraiah,{d} Jabish,{e} Gedaliah,{f} and all the honored men of the people. I led them to the Kidron{g} valley and told them everything I had been told.
They raised their voices and all wept.
We sat there and fasted until evening.

notes.text: "Zion" (Hebrew *Tsiyyon*) is the hill of Jerusalem on which the temple stood, and a poetic name for the city and its people.
"Jerusalem" (Hebrew *Yerushalayim*) is often explained as "foundation of peace" or "city of peace."
"Adu" appears only here and may be a copyist's form of another name; it is not found in the Bible. It is kept as written.
"Seraiah" (Hebrew *Serayah*) means "Yahweh has striven" or "Yahweh rules."
"Jabish" is not a name known from the Bible; the Hebrew *Yavesh* is related to "dry," as in Jabesh-gilead. It is kept as written.
"Gedaliah" (Hebrew *Gedalyahu*) means "Yahweh is great." A Gedaliah was appointed governor of Judah after the fall of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 40).
The "Kidron" (Hebrew *Qidron*), probably "dark" or "turbid," is the valley east of Jerusalem between the city and the Mount of Olives.

chapters.heading: Baruch's complaint, and God's reassurance

verses.text: The next day the army of the Chaldeans{a} surrounded the city. In the evening I, Baruch, left the people, went out, and stood beside the oak.
I was grieving over Zion and mourning the captivity that had come upon the people.
Suddenly a strong spirit lifted me and carried me up over the wall of Jerusalem.
I looked, and there were four angels standing at the four corners of the city, each holding a blazing torch.
Another angel began to come down from heaven. He said to them, "Hold your lamps, and do not light them until I tell you.
I have been sent first, to speak a word to the earth and to put into it what the Lord, the Most High, has ordered me to give."

I saw him go down into the Holy of Holies and take from it the veil, the holy ark, the mercy seat, the two tablets, the holy garments of the priests, the altar of incense, the forty-eight precious stones with which the priest was adorned, and all the holy furnishings of the tent.

He called to the earth in a loud voice, "Earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the mighty God! Receive what I entrust to you, and guard it until the last times, so that when you are ordered you may give it back, and strangers may not take possession of it.
For the time is coming when Jerusalem too will be handed over for a while, until it is said that she is restored forever."
Then the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them.

notes.text: "Chaldeans" (Hebrew *Kasdim*) is the Bible's name for the Babylonians.

chapters.heading: The Chaldeans invade; the sacred vessels are hidden

verses.text: After this I heard that angel say to the angels holding the lamps, "Now destroy the wall and throw it down to its foundations, so that the enemy cannot boast and say, 'We have thrown down the wall of Zion and burned the place of the mighty God.'"
And they took the place where I had been standing.
The angels did as he had ordered. When they had broken down the corners of the walls, a voice was heard from inside the temple after the wall had fallen. It said,
"Come in, you enemies; come, you adversaries! The One who guarded the house has left it."
Then I, Baruch, went away.

After this the Chaldean army entered, seized the house and everything around it, led the people off as captives, killed some of them, and bound King Zedekiah{a} and sent him to the king of Babylon{b}.

notes.text: "Zedekiah" (Hebrew *Tsidqiyyahu*) means "Yahweh is my righteousness." He was the last king of Judah.
"Babylon" (Hebrew *Bavel*) is linked in Genesis 11 with "confusion," from the verb *balal*. The Babylonians themselves understood it as "gate of God."

verses.text: Then I, Baruch, came with Jeremiah, whose heart was found pure of sin and who had not been taken when the city was seized.
We tore our clothes, wept, mourned, and fasted for seven days.

chapters.heading: A seven-day fast; Jeremiah goes with the exiles

verses.text: After seven days the word of God came to me and said,
"Tell Jeremiah to go and support the people in their captivity in Babylon. But you stay here among the ruins of Zion, and after these days I will show you what will happen at the end of days."
I told Jeremiah as the Lord had commanded.
He left with the people.
But I, Baruch, went back and sat in front of the gates of the temple, and I sang this lament over Zion:
"Blessed is the one who was never born, or the one who was born and has died.
But for us who live, woe! We see Zion's sufferings and what has happened to Jerusalem.

I will call the sirens from the sea. Come, Lilin,{a} from the desert, and you Shedim{b} and dragons from the forests. Wake up, tie up your clothes for mourning, take up the dirges with me, and lament with me.
Farmers, do not sow again. Earth, why give your harvest of fruit? Keep the sweet things of your food within you.
And you, vine, why give wine any more? No offering will ever again be made from you in Zion, and firstfruits will no longer be brought.
Heavens, hold back your dew and do not open the storehouses of rain.
Sun, hold back the light of your rays; moon, put out the multitude of your light. For why should light rise again where the light of Zion is darkened?
Bridegrooms, do not go in. Brides, do not put on wreaths. Women, do not pray to bear children.
For the childless will be happier than anyone, and those with no sons will be glad, and those with sons will be in anguish.
Why should they give birth in pain, only to bury in grief?
Why should the human race bear sons again, or why should the line of their kind be named again, when this mother lies desolate and her sons are led off into captivity?
From now on, do not speak of beauty and do not talk of grace.
Priests, take the keys of the sanctuary and throw them high into heaven. Give them to the Lord and say, "Guard Your own house, for we have turned out to be false stewards."

And you, virgins who weave fine linen and silk with gold from Ophir,{c} take all these things quickly and throw them into the fire, so that the fire may carry them to the One who made them, and the flame may send them to the One who created them, and the enemy may not take them.

notes.text: The Syriac has "Lilin," feminine night-creatures of Jewish folklore, related to the Hebrew *lilith* ("night creature") in Isaiah 34:14.
"Shedim" (Hebrew *shedim*) are demons or spirits; the word occurs in Deuteronomy 32:17 and Psalm 106:37.
"Ophir" is a land famous for its gold (1 Kings 9); its location is unknown, and some place it in southern Arabia, East Africa, or India. The name is kept as written.

verses.text: "I also say this against you, Babylon. If you had prospered while Zion lived in her glory, our grief would still have been great, to see you made equal to Zion.
But now the grief is endless and the mourning has no measure, for you flourish and Zion is desolate.
Who will judge these things? To whom shall we bring our complaint about what has happened to us? Lord, how have You endured it?
Our fathers went to rest without grief, and the righteous sleep in the earth in peace.
They did not know this anguish, and they had not heard what has happened to us.
If only you had ears, earth, and a heart, dust, so that you could go and tell Sheol,{a} and say to the dead,
'You are more blessed than we who live.'"

notes.text: "Sheol" is the Hebrew name for the place of the dead.

verses.text: "But I will say what I think, and I will speak against you, land, that now prospers.
The noonday sun does not burn all the time, and its rays do not always give light.
Do not expect to stay prosperous and joyful forever, and do not be so proud and boastful.
For in its own season the wrath of God will surely wake against you, though now, in His patience, it is held back as if by reins."
When I had said all this, I fasted for seven days.
After this I, Baruch, was standing on Mount Zion, and a voice came from on high and said to me,
"Stand on your feet, Baruch, and hear the word of the mighty God.
You were stunned at what has happened to Zion, and for that very reason you will be kept safe until the end of the times, to serve as a witness.
Then, if those prosperous cities ever say,

'Why has the mighty God brought this punishment on us?' you and those like you who have seen this disaster will tell them, 'This is the evil, and this is the punishment, that is coming on you and your people at its appointed time, so that the nations may be thoroughly struck down.'
Then they will be in anguish.
And if they say at that time,
'How long?' you will tell them, 'You who drank the strained wine, now drink its dregs as well. That is the judgment of the Most High, who shows no favoritism.'
For that reason He had no mercy on His own sons in earlier times, but treated them as enemies because they sinned.
So they were disciplined, in order to be made holy.
But now, you peoples and nations, you are guilty, because you have always trampled the earth and misused creation.
For I have always done you good, and you have always been ungrateful for it."

chapters.heading: A second fast; judgment on the nations

verses.text: I answered, "You have shown me how the times will run and what will come after them, and You have told me that the punishment You have spoken of will fall on the nations.
Now I know that those who have sinned are many, and they lived in comfort and then left the world. But few nations will be left in those times to hear the words You have spoken.
What good is it to us, or what could be worse than what we have already seen happen to us, that we should wait to see it?
But let me speak again before You.
What have they gained who knew You and did not walk in emptiness like the other nations, who never said to the dead, 'Give us life,' but always feared You and never left Your ways?
Yet they have been swept away, and You have shown Zion no mercy on their account.

If others did evil, it was for Zion's sake that she should have been forgiven, on account of the works of those who did good, and she should not have been overwhelmed on account of the works of those who did wrong.
But who, O Lord, my Lord, can grasp Your judgment? Who can search out the depth of Your way? Who can think through the weight of Your path?
Who can take in Your unfathomable counsel? Which of those who are born has ever found the beginning or the end of Your wisdom?
For we have all been made like a breath.
As breath goes up unasked and dies away again, so it is with human nature. We do not leave by our own will, and we do not know what will happen to us at the end.
The righteous rightly look forward to the end, and they leave this dwelling without fear, because they have a store of works laid up with You in treasuries.
So they leave this world without fear, and with joy they hope to receive the world You have promised them.
But we are in trouble: we are shamefully treated now, and in that time we look ahead to nothing but disasters.
You know exactly what You have done through Your servants, but we cannot understand what is good, as You, our Creator, do.
Let me speak once more before You, O Lord, my Lord.
Long ago, when there was no world with people in it, You planned and spoke by a word, and at once the works of creation stood before You.
You said that You would make humankind the steward of Your works, so that it might be known that humankind was not made for the sake of the world, but the world for the sake of humankind.
Now I see that the world made for our sake is still here, but we, for whom it was made, are going away."

chapters.heading: Why the righteous perish; God's answer

verses.text: The Lord answered me, "You are right to be amazed at the departure of human beings, but you have not judged well the evils that come on those who sin.
As for what you said, that the righteous are taken away while the wicked prosper,
and what you said, that a man does not know Your judgment,
listen, and I will speak to you; pay attention, and I will let you hear My words.
A man would not have understood My judgment rightly unless he had received the law and I had taught him understanding.
But he broke it knowingly, and for that very reason, because he knew, he will be tormented.
As for what you said about the righteous, that this world came into being on their account, so also the world to come will come on their account.
For to them this world is a struggle and a labor with much trouble, and the world that is coming is a crown with great glory."
I answered, "O Lord, my Lord, the years of this time are few and bad. Who can win in his short time what has no measure?"
The Lord answered me, "With the Most High, time and a few years are not counted.

What good did it do Adam that he lived nine hundred and thirty years and still broke what he was told? His long life did not help him. It brought death and cut short the years of all who were born from him. And what did Moses lose by living only a hundred and twenty years? Because he stayed under the One who formed him, he brought the law to the seed of Jacob{a} and lit a lamp for the nation of Israel."

notes.text: "Jacob" (Hebrew *Yaaqov*) is explained as "he grasps the heel" or "he supplants."

verses.text: I answered, "The one who lit the lamp took from the light, and few have followed him. But the many he lit it for took from the darkness of Adam and did not rejoice in the light of the lamp."
He answered me, "At that time He set a covenant before them and said, 'See, I have put before you life and death.' And He called heaven and earth to witness against them.
For He knew that His own time was short, but that heaven and earth last forever.
After his death they sinned and broke the covenant, though they knew they had the law to correct them, and the light in which nothing could go wrong, and the heavenly spheres that testify, and Me.
About everything that exists, I am the one who judges. Do not argue about these things in your soul, and do not torment yourself over what has already happened.
What now needs to be weighed is the end of the time, whether of business, of prosperity, or of shame, and not its beginning.
If a man does well at the start and is treated shamefully in his old age, he forgets all the good he had.
And if a man is treated shamefully at the start and does well at the end, he does not remember his earlier mistreatment.
Listen again. Suppose each person did well for all that time, from the day death was decreed against those who disobey, and then was destroyed at the end. Everything would have been in vain."
"So see, the days are coming, and the times will move faster than before, and the seasons will hurry along faster than those that are past, and the years will go by faster than the present ones.
That is why I have now taken Zion away, so that I may visit the world sooner, in its season.
Now hold on to everything I command you, and seal it in the hidden places of your mind.
Then I will show you the judgment of My power and My ways that cannot be searched out.
Go and make yourself holy for seven days. Eat no bread, drink no water, and speak to no one.
After that, come to that place, and I will reveal Myself to you and speak true things with you. I will give you commands about how the times run, for they are coming and will not wait."

chapters.heading: Zion has been taken away to hasten the judgment

verses.text: I went there and sat in the Kidron valley in an earth cave, and I made my soul holy. I ate no bread, yet I was not hungry. I drank no water, yet I was not thirsty. I stayed there until the seventh day, as He had commanded me.
Then I came to the place where He had spoken with me.
At sunset my soul was deep in thought, and I began to speak in the presence of the Mighty One. I said,
"You who made the earth, hear me! You fixed the sky by a word and set the height of heaven firm by Your spirit. From the beginning You called what did not yet exist, and it obeys You.
You commanded the air with a nod, and You see what is yet to be as clearly as what You are doing now.

You rule with great purpose the hosts that stand before You, and the countless holy beings that You made from the beginning, made of flame and fire, who stand around Your throne; You rule them with fierce force.
It belongs to You alone to do at once whatever You wish.
You make the raindrops fall on the earth by number, and You alone know the end of the times before they come. Look kindly on my prayer.
For You alone can sustain all who are, those who have passed away and those who are yet to be, those who sin and those who are righteous, as living beings who cannot be fully known.
For You alone live forever, beyond all searching out, and You know the number of mankind.
And if in time many have sinned, others, not a few, have been righteous.
You know where You keep the end of those who sinned and the final reward of those who were righteous.
For if there were only this life, which belongs to everyone, nothing could be more bitter.
What use is strength that turns to sickness, or a full table that turns to famine, or beauty that turns to ugliness?
For human nature is always changing.
What we were before, we no longer are; and what we are now, we will not stay.
If an end had not been prepared for all, their beginning would have been pointless.
But tell me about everything that comes from You, and shed light on everything I ask You.
How long will what decays go on? How long will mortals prosper? And until when will those who sin in the world be stained with so much wickedness?
Command it in mercy and carry out everything You said You would bring, so that Your power may be known to those who think Your patience is weakness.
Show those who do not know that all that has happened to us and to our city until now has been within the patience of Your power, because for Your name's sake You called us a beloved people.
Put an end to death from now on.

Rebuke the angel of death, and let Your glory appear, and let the might of Your beauty be known. Let Sheol be sealed so that from now on it takes in no more dead, and let the storehouses of souls give back those shut up in them.
For many years have been like desolate ones since the days of Abraham, Isaac{a}, Jacob, and all who are like them, who sleep in the earth, those for whose sake You said You created the world.
Now show Your glory quickly, and do not put off what You promised."
When I finished the words of this prayer, I was very weak.

notes.text: "Isaac" (Hebrew *Yitschaq*) means "he laughs."

chapters.heading: Baruch's prayer, and God's answer

verses.text: After this, the heavens opened, and I saw, and power was given to me, and a voice from on high said to me,
"Baruch, Baruch, why are you troubled?
If someone sets out on a road and does not finish it, or leaves by sea and does not reach harbor, can he be comforted?
If someone promises a gift to another and does not give it, is that not robbery?
If someone sows a field and does not reap its fruit in season, does he not lose everything?
If someone plants a plant and it does not grow until its time, can the one who planted it expect fruit from it?
If a woman conceives and gives birth too early, does she not surely kill her child?
If someone builds a house and does not roof it and finish it, can it be called a house? Tell Me that first."
I answered, "Surely not, O Lord, my Lord."
He answered me, "Then why are you troubled about what you do not know, and uneasy about things of which you are ignorant?
Just as you have not forgotten the people who now live and those who have passed away, so I remember those who are appointed to come.

When Adam sinned and death was decreed against all who would be born, the number of those to be born was counted, and a place was prepared for that number, where the living might live and the dead might be kept.
Before that number is complete, the creature will not live again, for My Spirit is the creator of life, and Sheol will receive the dead.
And again, it is given to you to hear what will come after these times.
For My redemption has truly come near; it is not far off as it was before."

"See, the days are coming when the books will be opened in which the sins of all who have sinned are written, and also the storehouses in which the righteousness of all who have been righteous in creation is gathered.

At that time you will see, and many with you, the patience of the Most High, which has lasted through all generations, patient toward all who are born, those who sin and those who are righteous alike."
I answered, "But, Lord, no one knows the number of what has passed or of what is still to come.
I know indeed what has happened to us, but what will happen to our enemies I do not know, or when You will visit Your works."

chapters.heading: The coming judgment

verses.text: He answered me, "You too will be kept until that time, until the sign that the Most High will give to the people of the earth at the end of days.
This will be the sign.
When a stupor takes hold of the people of the earth and they fall into many troubles, and then again into great torments,
they will say in their thoughts, because of all their suffering, 'The Mighty One no longer remembers the earth.' Yes, when they give up hope, then the time will wake."

chapters.heading: The sign of the coming judgment

verses.text: I answered, "Will that tribulation last a long time? Will that hardship go on for many years?"
He answered me, "That time is divided into twelve parts, and each is kept for what is assigned to it.
In the first part there will be the beginning of unrest.
In the second part, the killing of great men.
In the third part, the fall of many through death.
In the fourth part, the sending of the sword.
In the fifth part, famine and the holding back of rain.
In the sixth part, earthquakes and terrors.
The seventh part is missing in the Syriac text.{a}
In the eighth part, a crowd of ghosts and attacks by the Shedim.
In the ninth part, the falling of fire.
In the tenth part, plunder and heavy oppression.
In the eleventh part, wickedness and sexual wrongdoing.
In the twelfth part, confusion from the mixing together of all the things just named.
These parts of that time are held in reserve, and they will mingle with one another and serve one another.

Some will leave out part of their own and take from others, and some will finish their own and others' as well, so that those living on the earth in those days will not understand that this is the end of the times."

notes.text: The seventh part is missing in the Syriac manuscript; nothing is supplied here, and the list resumes at the eighth.

chapters.heading: The twelve woes, the Messiah, and the temporary Messianic kingdom

verses.text: "Even so, whoever understands will be wise then.
The measure and count of that time is two parts of a week of seven weeks."
I answered, "It is good for a man to come and see, but better that he not come, lest he fall.
But I will also say this.
Will someone who is incorruptible look down on things that are corruptible, and on whatever happens to them, so that he looks only at what is not corruptible?
But if, Lord, what You have told me will surely come to pass, then show me this as well, if I have found favor with You.
Will these things take place in one place, or in one part of the earth, or will the whole earth experience them?"
He answered me, "Whatever will happen then will happen to the whole earth, so all who live will experience it.
At that time I will protect only those who are found in this land in those very days.
When everything that was to happen in those parts has been done, the Messiah will begin to be revealed.

Behemoth{a} will be revealed from his place, and Leviathan{b} will rise from the sea, the two great monsters I made on the fifth day of creation and have kept until that time. Then they will be food for all who are left.

The earth will yield its fruit ten-thousandfold. Each vine will have a thousand branches, each branch will bear a thousand clusters, each cluster a thousand grapes, and each grape will give a cor{c} of wine, about 55 gallons.
Those who were hungry will rejoice, and every day they will see marvels.
Winds will go out from Me every morning to bring the fragrance of spice-bearing fruits, and at the end of each day, clouds that let fall the dew of health.
At that same time the storehouse of manna will again come down from on high, and they will eat of it in those years, because these are the ones who have come to the end of the age."

notes.text: "Behemoth" (Hebrew *behemot*) is the great land beast of Job 40:15-24.
"Leviathan" (Hebrew *livyatan*) is the sea monster of Job 41 and Psalm 74:14.
The Syriac has *cor*, a Hebrew dry and liquid measure (*kor*). It is usually reckoned at roughly 45 to 60 gallons (170 to 230 liters); the figure given in the text is an approximation.

verses.text: "After this, when the time of the Messiah's coming is fulfilled, he will return in glory.

Then all who have fallen asleep in hope of him will rise. At that time the storehouses will be opened in which the number of the souls of the righteous is kept, and they will come out, and a crowd of souls will be seen together in one gathering, of one mind. The first will be glad and the last will not be sad.
For they know that the time has come of which it is said that it is the end of the times.
But the souls of the wicked, when they see all this, will waste away all the more.
For they will know that their torment has come and their ruin has arrived."

chapters.heading: The resurrection

verses.text: After this I went to the people and said to them, "Gather all your elders to me, and I will speak words to them."
They all gathered in the Kidron valley.
I answered and said to them, "Hear, Israel, and I will speak to you; listen, seed of Jacob, and I will teach you.
Do not forget Zion, but keep the anguish of Jerusalem in mind.
For the days are coming when everything that exists will become prey to corruption, and will be as though it had never been."

chapters.heading: Baruch urges the people to prepare

verses.text: "But if you prepare your hearts, so that you sow the fruits of the law in them, it will protect you in that time when the Mighty One is going to shake the whole creation.
After a little while the building of Zion will be shaken so that it can be built again.
But that building will not last. After a time it will be uprooted again and stay desolate until the appointed time.
Afterward it must be renewed in glory and made perfect forever.
So we should not grieve as much over the evil that has come now as over the one that is still to come.
For there will be a greater trial than these two tribulations, when the Mighty One renews His creation.
Now do not come near me for a few days, and do not look for me until I come to you."
When I had said all this to them, I, Baruch, went my way. When the people saw me leaving, they raised their voices, wept, and said,
"Where are you going, Baruch? Are you abandoning us like a father who abandons his orphaned children and leaves them?"
"Are these the orders your companion Jeremiah the prophet gave you when he said to you,
'Look after these people until I go and prepare the rest of the brothers in Babylon, who have been sentenced to be taken into captivity'?
Now if you also leave us, it would be better for us all to die before you, and then for you to leave us."

I answered the people, "Far be it from me to leave you or withdraw from you. I will only go to the Holy of Holies to ask the Mighty One about you and about Zion, in case I may receive more light. After this I will come back to you."

chapters.heading: Baruch's lament

verses.text: I, Baruch, went to the holy place, sat down on the ruins, wept, and said,
"If only my eyes were springs and my eyelids a fountain of tears.
How can I lament for Zion? How can I mourn for Jerusalem?
In the place where I now lie face down, the high priest once offered holy sacrifices and placed on it incense of fragrant spices.
Now our pride has been turned to dust, and the desire of our soul to sand."
When I had said this, I fell asleep there, and in the night I saw a vision.
There was a forest of trees planted on a plain, and tall, rugged, rocky mountains surrounded it. That forest took up a lot of room.
Then, facing it, a vine rose up, and from beneath it a spring flowed out peacefully.
The spring came to the forest and rose into great waves. The waves flooded the forest, and suddenly they tore up most of it and knocked down all the mountains around it.
The tops of the forest began to be brought low, and the peaks of the mountains were made low, and the spring was so strong that it left nothing of that great forest except one cedar.

When it had thrown that forest down and destroyed and uprooted most of it, so that nothing was left and even its place could not be recognized, the vine came with the spring, in peace and great calm, to a place not far from the cedar. They brought the fallen cedar to the vine.

I looked, and the vine opened its mouth and spoke to the cedar. It said, "Are you not the cedar that was left from the forest of wickedness, through whom wickedness lasted and was done all those years, and goodness never?

You kept conquering what was not yours, and you never showed compassion to what was yours. You kept stretching your power over those far from you, and you held those who came near you fast in the traps of your wickedness. You always lifted yourself up as if you could never be torn out!
But now your time has run out and your hour has come.
So you also depart, cedar, after the forest that went before you, and turn to dust with it, and let your ashes be mixed together.
Now lie down in anguish and rest in torment until your last time comes, when you will come again and be tormented still more."

chapters.heading: The vision of the forest, the vine, the fountain, and the cedar

verses.text: After this I saw that cedar burning and the vine growing, with the plain around it full of flowers that never fade.
Then I woke up and got up.
I prayed and said, "O Lord, my Lord, You always give light to those who are led by understanding.
Your law is life, and Your wisdom is the right way.
So make known to me the meaning of this vision.
You know that my soul has always walked in Your law, and from my earliest days I never left Your wisdom."

chapters.heading: The vision explained

verses.text: He answered me, "Baruch, this is the meaning of the vision you saw.
You saw the great forest surrounded by tall, rugged mountains. This is what it means.
See, the days are coming when this kingdom, which once destroyed Zion, will itself be destroyed and made subject to the one that comes after it.
After a time that one too will be destroyed, and another, a third, will rise, and it will also hold power for its time and be destroyed.

After this a fourth kingdom will rise, whose power will be harsher and more evil than any before it. It will rule for many times as long as the forests on the plain, hold on for ages, and lift itself higher than the cedars of Lebanon{a}.
Truth will be hidden by it, and all who are stained with wrongdoing will flee to it, as wild beasts flee and creep into a forest.
When the time comes near for it to fall, then the rule of My Messiah will be revealed, which is like the spring and the vine. When it is revealed, it will tear out the multitude of its army.
As for the tall cedar left over from that forest, and the vine speaking to it the words you heard, this is what it means."

notes.text: "Lebanon" (Hebrew *Levanon*) means "white," perhaps for its snowy peaks.

verses.text: "The last ruler of that time will be left alive after the multitude of his armies has been put to the sword. He will be bound, and they will take him up to Mount Zion, and My Messiah will convict him of all his godless deeds. He will gather and set before him all the works of his armies.
Afterward he will put him to death and protect the rest of My people, who will be found in the place I have chosen.
His rule will stand forever, until the world of corruption comes to an end and the times I have mentioned are fulfilled.
This is your vision, and this is what it means."
I answered, "For whom, and for how many, will these things be? Who will be worthy to live at that time?
I will say before You everything I am thinking, and I will ask You about what I am pondering.
I see many of Your people who have turned from Your covenant and thrown off the yoke of Your law.
But I have seen others who gave up their emptiness and fled for shelter under Your wings.
What will happen to them? How will the last time receive them?
Or perhaps their time will be weighed, and they will be judged as the balance tips?"

chapters.heading: The apostates and the converts

verses.text: He answered me, "I will show you this too.
As for what you said, 'For whom will these things be, and for how many?' To those who have believed, the good that was promised long ago will come, and to those who despise it, the opposite.
As for what you said about those who have drawn near and those who have withdrawn, this is the answer.
Those who were first subject to Me and afterward turned away and mingled with the seed of mixed peoples: the time of these was the former time, and it was counted as something exalted.

And those who did not know before, but afterward came to know life and mingled only with the seed of the people that had set itself apart: the time of these is the latter time, and it is counted as something exalted.

Time will follow time and season will follow season. One will receive from another, and then, with the end in view, everything will be compared by the measure of the times and the hours of the seasons.
For corruption will take what belongs to it, and life will take what belongs to it.
The dust will be called and told, 'Give back what is not yours, and raise up everything you have kept until its time.'"
"But you, Baruch, turn your heart to what has been said to you, and understand what has been shown to you, for there are many everlasting comforts for you.
You will leave this place and pass from the regions you now see. You will forget whatever is corruptible and will no longer remember what happens among mortals.
So go and command your people, and come to this place. After that, fast for seven days, and then I will come to you and speak with you."

chapters.heading: Baruch is told of his death

verses.text: I, Baruch, went from there and came to my people. I called my firstborn son, and the Gedaliahs, my friends, and seven of the elders of the people, and I said to them,
"See, I am going to my fathers, the way of all the earth.
But do not leave the way of the law. Guard the people who remain and warn them, so that they do not turn from the commands of the Mighty One.
You see that the One we serve is just, and that our Creator shows no favoritism.
See what has happened to Zion, and what has come upon Jerusalem.
By this the judgment of the Mighty One will be made known, and His ways, which cannot be traced out yet are right.
If you endure and keep on in His fear and do not forget His law, the times will change for the better over you, and you will see the comfort of Zion.
For whatever exists now is nothing, but what is to come is very great.
Everything corruptible will pass away and everything that dies will go. All the present time will be forgotten, and there will be no memory of the present time, which is stained with evils.
For what runs on now runs toward emptiness, and what prospers will quickly fall and be humbled.
What is to come will be the object of desire, and we will hope for what comes after. It is a time that does not pass away.

The hour comes that lasts forever, and the new world comes, which does not turn to corruption those who go to its blessing, has no mercy on those who go to torment, and does not lead to ruin those who live in it.
These are the ones who will inherit the time that has been spoken of, and theirs is the inheritance of the promised time.

These are the ones who have gathered for themselves treasures of wisdom, and with them are found stores of understanding. They have not turned away from mercy, and they have kept the truth of the law.
To them the world to come will be given, but the dwelling of the rest, who are many, will be in the fire."

chapters.heading: Baruch tells the elders of his coming death

verses.text: "So, as far as you can, teach the people, for that work is ours.
If you teach them, you will give them life."
My son and the elders of the people answered me, "Has the Mighty One humbled us so much as to take you from us so quickly?
We will truly be in darkness, with no light for the people who are left.
Where will we look for the law again, and who will tell us the difference between death and life?"
I said to them, "I cannot resist the throne of the Mighty One. Even so, Israel will never lack a wise man, nor the family of Jacob a son of the law.
Only prepare your hearts to obey the law, and be subject to those who are wise and understanding in fear of Him. Prepare your souls so that you do not leave them.
If you do these things, good news will come to you.
That is what I told you before, and you will not fall into the torment of which I warned you earlier.
But about the word that I was to be taken, I did not tell them or my son.
When I had gone out and sent them away, I went there and said to them, "See, I am going to Hebron{a}, for the Mighty One has sent me there."
I came to the place where the word had been spoken to me, sat there, and fasted for seven days.

notes.text: "Hebron" (Hebrew *Chevron*) is related to "association" or "league." It is a city in the hills south of Jerusalem.

verses.text: After the seventh day I prayed before the Mighty One and said,
"O my Lord, You call the coming of the times, and they stand before You. You make the power of the ages pass away, and they do not resist You. You set the order of the seasons, and they obey You.
You alone know how long the generations last, and You do not reveal Your mysteries to many.
You make known how great the fire is, and You weigh how light the wind is.
You search out the limits of the heights, and You examine the depths of the darkness.
You look after the number of those who pass away, so that they may be kept, and You prepare a home for those who are to come.
You remember the beginning that You made, and You do not forget the destruction that is to come.
At Your nod, in fear and anger, You command the flames, and they change into spirits. With a word You bring to life what was not, and with mighty power You hold back what has not yet come.
You teach created things to understand You, and You make the heavenly spheres wise so that they serve in their ranks.
Countless armies stand before You and quietly serve in their ranks at Your nod.
Hear Your servant and listen to my plea.
We are born in a short time, and in a short time we return.
But with You hours are like an age, and days are like generations.
So do not be angry with humanity, for it is nothing,
and do not hold our deeds against us. What are we? It is by Your gift that we come into the world, and we do not leave by our own will.
We never said to our parents, 'Give birth to us,' and we never sent word to Sheol, saying, 'Take us in.'
What is our strength, that we could bear Your wrath? What are we, that we could stand Your judgment?
Shelter us in Your compassion, and help us in Your mercy.
Look at the little ones who are subject to You, and save everyone who comes near You. Do not destroy our people's hope, and do not cut short the times of our help.
This is the nation You chose, and these are the people for whom You find no equal.
But now I will speak before You and say what my heart thinks.
We trust in You, for Your law is with us, and we know that we will not fall as long as we keep Your statutes.
We are blessed forever in this at least, that we have not mingled with the nations.
For we are all one famous people who received one law from the One. The law among us will help us, and the surpassing wisdom in us will assist us."
When I had prayed and said these things, I was greatly weakened.
He answered me, "You have prayed simply, Baruch, and all your words have been heard.
But My judgment claims what is its own, and My law claims its rights.
I will answer you from your own words, and speak to you from your own prayer.
It is like this: one who is corrupted is no more. He has done wrong as far as he was able, and he has not remembered My goodness or accepted My patience.
So you will surely be taken up, as I told you before.
For a time will rise that brings affliction. It will come and pass by with swift violence, and it will be stormy, coming in the heat of anger.
In those days all the inhabitants of the earth will be stirred up against one another, because they do not know that My judgment has come near.
Not many wise people will be found in that time, and the intelligent will be only a few. Even those who know will mostly stay silent.
There will be many rumors and plenty of news. Illusions will be seen at work, and many promises will be told. Some will turn out empty, and some will be confirmed.
Honor will turn into shame, strength will be crushed into contempt, integrity will be destroyed, and beauty will become ugliness.
In that time many will say to many, 'Where has the multitude of understanding hidden itself, and where has the multitude of wisdom gone?'

While they are thinking this over, envy will rise in those who thought nothing of themselves, and passion will seize the peaceful. Many will be stirred up in anger to hurt many, and they will raise armies to shed blood, and in the end they will perish along with them.

At that same time a change of the times will be plain to everyone, because throughout those times they made themselves unclean, practiced oppression, each walked in his own works, and did not remember the law of the Mighty One.
So a fire will consume their thoughts, and in flames the plans of their inmost being will be tested. For the Judge will come and will not delay.
Each of the inhabitants of the earth knew when he was breaking the law, but in their pride they did not know My Law.
Then many will certainly weep, more over the living than over the dead."
I answered, "O Adam, what have you done to all those born from you? And what will be said to the first Eve{a}, who listened to the serpent?
This whole multitude is heading toward corruption, and there is no counting those the fire devours.
But I will speak again in Your presence.
You, O Lord, my Lord, know what is in Your creature.
Long ago You commanded the dust to bring forth Adam, and You know the number of those born from him, and how far they have sinned before You, who lived and did not confess You as their Creator.
As for all of these, their end will convict them, and Your law, which they broke, will repay them on Your day."
"But now let us set the wicked aside and ask about the righteous.
I will describe their blessedness and will not be silent in celebrating their glory, which is kept for them.
For just as you have endured much labor for a little time in this passing world where you live, so in that world that has no end you will receive great light."

notes.text: "Eve" (Hebrew *Chavvah*) is traditionally linked to "life" or "living."

chapters.heading: Baruch's prayer and the answer

verses.text: "Even so, I will ask You again, Mighty One, and I will ask You, who made all things.
In what form will those live who live in Your day? How will the splendor of those who come after that time continue?

Will they take on this present form again and put on these tangled limbs, which are now caught up in evils and in which evils reach their peak? Or will You perhaps change these things that have been in the world, just as You change the world?"

chapters.heading: The nature of the resurrection body

verses.text: He answered me, "Listen to this word, Baruch, and write in the memory of your heart everything you will learn.

The earth will then surely give back the dead, which it now receives to keep. It will make no change in their form, but as it received them, so it will return them. As I handed them over to it, so it will raise them.
For then it will be necessary to show the living that the dead have come back to life and that those who had departed have returned.
When they have each recognized those they know now, then the judgment will grow strong, and the things that were spoken of before will come."
"When that appointed day has passed, the appearance of those who are condemned will be changed, and so will the glory of those who are declared righteous.
The appearance of those who now do evil will become worse than it is, since they will suffer torment.

As for the glory of those who have now been made righteous in My law, who have had understanding in their lives and have planted the root of wisdom in their hearts, their splendor will be glorified in changes, and the form of their faces will be turned into the light of their beauty, so that they may gain and receive the world that does not die, which is then promised to them.
Above all, those who come then will grieve over this: that they rejected My law and stopped their ears so as not to hear wisdom or receive understanding.

When they see those whom they now look down on, who will then be lifted up and glorified more than they are, the righteous will be transformed into the splendor of angels, and the wicked will waste away still more in wonder at the sights and the forms they behold.
For they will see first, and afterward go away to be tormented.
But those who were saved by their works, for whom the law has been a hope, understanding an expectation, and wisdom a confidence, will see wonders appear in their time.
They will see the world that is now invisible to them, and they will see the time that is now hidden from them.
Time will no longer age them.

They will live in the heights of that world, and they will be made like the angels and equal to the stars. They will be changed into any form they wish, from beauty into loveliness, and from light into the splendor of glory.

The wide spaces of Paradise will be spread out before them, and the beauty of the majesty of the living creatures beneath the throne will be shown to them, along with all the armies of angels, who are now held back by My word so that they do not appear, and are held by a command to stand in their places until their coming arrives.
Moreover, there will then be an excellence in the righteous that surpasses that of the angels.
For the first will receive the last, whom they were expecting, and the last will receive those of whom they used to hear that they had passed away.
For they have been rescued from this world of tribulation and have laid down the burden of anguish.
What have people lost their lives for, and what have those on the earth traded their souls for?

They did not choose for themselves that time which, beyond the reach of anguish, could never pass away. They chose for themselves the time whose outcomes are full of lamentation and evil. They denied the world that does not age those who come to it, and they rejected the time of glory, so that they will not come to the honor of which I told you before."
I answered, "How could we forget those for whom woe is then kept in store?
Why, then, do we mourn again for those who die? Why do we weep for those who go down to Sheol?
Let the lamentations be kept for the start of that coming torment, and let the tears be stored up for the arrival of the destruction of that time.
But even in the face of these things I will speak.
And as for the righteous, what will they do now?
Rejoice in the suffering you now endure. Why do you look for the decline of your enemies?
Make your souls ready for what is kept for you, and prepare them for the reward laid up for you."

After I had said these things, I fell asleep there, and I saw a vision. A cloud was rising from a very great sea. I kept looking at it, and it was full of white and black waters, with many colors in those same waters, and at its top there was what looked like great lightning.
I saw the cloud moving swiftly in quick courses, and it covered all the earth.
After this the cloud began to pour out on the earth the waters it held.
I saw that the waters coming down from it were not all alike.
At the first they were black and many. Then I saw the waters become bright, but they were not many. After this I saw black waters again, then bright, then black again, and bright again.
This happened twelve times, but the black were always more numerous than the bright.
At the end of the cloud it rained black waters, darker than all the earlier waters, and fire was mixed with them. Where those waters came down, they brought devastation and destruction.
After this I saw the lightning I had seen at the top of the cloud seize the cloud and hurl it to the earth.
That lightning shone so brightly that it lit up the whole earth, and it healed the regions where the last waters had come down and brought devastation.
It took hold of the whole earth and ruled over it.
After this I saw twelve rivers rising from the sea, and they began to surround the lightning and become subject to it.
In my fear I woke up.

chapters.heading: The vision of the cloud with dark and bright waters

verses.text: I pleaded with the Mighty One and said, "You alone, Lord, know the deep things of the world from ages past. You bring about by Your word what happens in its times. In response to the works of the inhabitants of the earth You hurry the beginnings of the times, and You alone know the end of the seasons.
Nothing is too hard for You, and You do everything easily with a nod.
To You the depths are like the heights, and the beginnings of the ages serve Your word.
You reveal to those who fear You what is prepared for them, so that from then on they may be comforted.

You show great deeds to those who do not know. You break open the walls around the ignorant. You light up what is dark and reveal what is hidden to the pure, who in faith have submitted to You and Your law.
You have shown this vision to Your servant. Show me its meaning as well.
I know that I have received an answer about the things I asked, and in answer to my request You showed me with what voice to praise You and with what limbs to send up praises and hallelujahs to You.

Even if my limbs were mouths and the hairs of my head were voices, I still could not give You the praise You deserve, nor honor You as is fitting. I could not recount Your praise or tell the glory of Your beauty.
What am I among people, or why am I counted among those better than I am, that I have heard all these marvelous things from the Most High and countless promises from the One who made me?
Blessed be my mother among those who bear children, and praised among women be she who gave birth to me.
I will not be silent in praising the Mighty One, and with the voice of praise I will tell of His marvelous deeds.
Who does anything like Your marvelous deeds, O God? Who can grasp Your deep thought about life?
By Your counsel You govern all the creatures that Your right hand made. You set every fountain of light beside You, and You prepared the treasures of wisdom beneath Your throne.
Those who have not loved Your law rightly perish, and the torment of judgment awaits those who have not submitted to Your power.
Adam sinned first and brought early death on everyone, but of those born from him, each one has prepared torment to come for his own soul, and each has also chosen glories to come for himself.
Whoever believes will certainly receive a reward.
But as for you wicked ones who live now, go and turn toward destruction, because you will soon be visited, since you rejected the understanding of the Most High.
His works have not taught you, and the skill of His creation, always before you, has not persuaded you.
So Adam is not the cause except of his own soul, but each of us has become the Adam of his own soul.
But You, Lord, explain to me the things You have revealed to me, and tell me about what I asked You.
At the completion of the world, vengeance will be taken on those who have done wickedness, according to their wickedness, and You will glorify the faithful according to their faithfulness.
You rule over those who belong to You, and You blot out from among Your own those who sin."

chapters.heading: Baruch asks for the meaning of the vision

verses.text: When I had finished speaking the words of this prayer, I sat down there under a tree to rest in the shade of its branches.

I wondered and was amazed, and I thought about the abundance of goodness that sinners on the earth have rejected, and about the great torment they have despised, although they knew they would be tormented because of the sin they had committed.
While I was thinking about these and similar things, the angel Ramiel{a}, who is in charge of true visions, was sent to me, and he said to me,
"Baruch, why does your heart trouble you, and why does your thought disturb you?
If you are so moved by a mere report of the judgment, what will you do when you see it clearly with your own eyes?
If you are so overcome by waiting for the day of the Mighty One, what will you do when you come to its arrival?
If you are so completely distraught at the word announcing the torment of those who have acted foolishly, how much more when the event itself shows its marvels?
If you have heard news of the good and evil things that are then coming and are grieved, what will you do when you see what the Majesty will reveal, which will convict some and make others rejoice?"

notes.text: "Ramiel" (Hebrew *Remiel*) is thought to mean "thunder of God" or "God has raised up."

verses.text: "Since you asked the Most High to explain the vision you saw, I have been sent to tell you.

The Mighty One has truly made known to you the course of the times that have passed and those that are meant to pass in His world, from the beginning of its creation to its completion, both what is deceit and what is truth.
The great cloud you saw rising from the sea and going on to cover the earth is the duration of the world, which the Mighty One made when He decided to make the world.
When the word went out from His presence, the duration of the world came into being in a small way, and it was established according to the fullness of the understanding of the One who sent it.
The black waters you saw first at the top of the cloud, which came down on the earth first, are the transgression that Adam, the first man, committed.

For from the time he transgressed, early death came into being, grief was given a name, anguish was prepared, pain was created, trouble was brought to its height, and disease began to take hold. Sheol kept demanding to be renewed with blood. The bearing of children came about, the passion of parents arose, human greatness was brought low, and goodness withered.
What could be blacker or darker than these things?
This is the beginning of the black waters you saw.
From these black waters, black waters came again, and the darkness of darkness was produced.
He became a danger to his own soul, and even to the angels.
At that time, when he was created, they had enjoyed freedom.
Because he became a danger to them, some of them came down and mingled with the women.
Then those who did this were tormented in chains.
But the rest of the multitude of angels, who cannot be counted, held themselves back.
Those who lived on the earth perished together with them in the waters of the flood.
These are the first black waters."

chapters.heading: Interpretation: the dark and bright waters

verses.text: "After these waters you saw bright waters. This is the fountain of Abraham, together with his generations and the coming of his son and his son's son, and of those like them.

At that time the unwritten law was known among them, the works of the commandments were fulfilled, belief in the coming judgment arose, hope in the world that was to be renewed was built up, and the promise of the life to come was planted.
These are the bright waters you saw."

"The black third waters you saw are the mixing together of all sins that the nations committed after the death of those righteous men, and the wickedness of the land of Egypt{a}, where they acted wickedly in the service by which they made their sons serve.
Yet even these perished in the end."

notes.text: "Egypt" translates the Hebrew *Mitsrayim*, of uncertain meaning.

verses.text: "The bright fourth waters you saw are the coming of Moses, Aaron{a}, Miriam{b}, Joshua{c} son of Nun, Caleb{d}, and all those like them.
At that time the lamp of the eternal law shone on all who sat in darkness. It announced the promised reward to those who believe, and the torment of fire kept for them to those who deny.
At that time even the heavens were shaken from their place, and those under the throne of the Mighty One were disturbed when He took Moses to Himself.

He showed him many warnings, together with the principles of the law and the end of the times, as He has to you also, and likewise the pattern of Zion and its measurements, on the pattern of which the sanctuary of the present time was to be made.
He also showed him the extent of the fire, the depths of the abyss, the weight of the winds, and the number of the drops of rain,
the restraint of anger, the abundance of patience, and the truth of judgment,
the root of wisdom, the riches of understanding, and the spring of knowledge,
the height of the air, the greatness of Paradise, the end of the ages, and the start of the day of judgment,
the number of the offerings, and the worlds that have not yet come,
the mouth of Gehenna, the place where vengeance stands, the place of faith, and the region of hope,

the likeness of future torment, the multitude of countless angels, the flaming hosts, the splendor of the lightnings, the voice of the thunders, the ranks of the chief angels, the treasuries of light, the changes of the times, and the study of the law.
These are the bright fourth waters you saw."

notes.text: "Aaron" (Hebrew *Aharon*) is of uncertain meaning.
"Miriam" (Hebrew *Miryam*) is of uncertain meaning; it may be related to "bitter" or "beloved."
"Joshua" (Hebrew *Yehoshua*) means "Yahweh saves."
"Caleb" (Hebrew *Kalev*) is often taken to mean "dog" or "wholehearted."

verses.text: "The black fifth waters you saw raining are the works the Amorites did, the spells of their incantations, the wickedness of their mysteries, and the mixing of their pollution.
Even Israel was defiled by sins in the days of the judges, although they saw many signs from the One who made them."
"The bright sixth waters you saw are the time when David{a} and Solomon{b} were born.
At that time Zion was built, the sanctuary was dedicated, much blood of the nations that sinned then was shed, and many offerings were made at the dedication of the sanctuary.
There was peace and calm at that time.
Wisdom was heard in the assembly, and the riches of understanding were honored in the congregations.
The holy festivals were kept in blessing and great joy.
The judgment of the rulers was seen to be without deceit, and the righteousness of the Mighty One's precepts was carried out in truth.
The land was loved by the Lord at that time, and because its inhabitants did not sin, it was glorified above all lands, and the city of Zion ruled over all lands and regions.
These are the bright waters you saw."

notes.text: "David" (Hebrew *David*) probably means "beloved."
"Solomon" (Hebrew *Shelomoh*) is related to *shalom*, "peace."

verses.text: "The black seventh waters you saw are the perversion that came from the plan of Jeroboam{a}, who planned to make two golden calves,
and all the wrongdoing that the kings after him did wickedly.
They are the curse of Jezebel{b} and the worship of idols that Israel practiced at that time,
the withholding of rain, and the famines that happened until women ate the fruit of their own wombs,
and the time of captivity that came on the nine and a half tribes, because they were in many sins.
Shalmaneser{c}, king of Assyria{d}, came and led them away captive.
As for the nations, it would be tiresome to tell how they always practiced ungodliness and wickedness and never did righteousness.
These are the black seventh waters you saw."

notes.text: "Jeroboam" (Hebrew *Yarovam*) is usually explained as "the people contend" or "may the kinsman increase."
"Jezebel" (Hebrew *Izevel*) is a Phoenician name, perhaps meaning "where is the prince?"
"Shalmaneser" (Assyrian *Shulmanu-asharedu*) means "Shulmanu is foremost."
"Assyria" (Hebrew *Ashshur*) is named for its chief city and god, Ashur.

verses.text: "The bright eighth waters you saw are the uprightness and honesty of Hezekiah{a}, king of Judah, and the grace that came upon him.
For Sennacherib{b} was stirred up, so that he would perish, and his rage troubled him, so that he would perish by it, together with the multitude of the nations that were with him.

When King Hezekiah heard what the king of Assyria was planning, which was to come and seize him and destroy his people, the two and a half tribes that remained, and even to overthrow Zion also, Hezekiah trusted in his works and hoped in his righteousness, and he spoke with the Mighty One and said,
'See, Sennacherib is ready to destroy us, and he will be boastful and proud when he has destroyed Zion.'
The Mighty One heard him, for Hezekiah was wise, and He paid attention to his prayer because he was righteous.
Then the Mighty One gave orders to Ramiel, His angel who speaks with you.
And I went out and destroyed their multitude, the number of whose commanders alone was one hundred eighty-five thousand, and each of them had an equal number under him.

At that time I burned their bodies inside, but I kept their clothes and weapons untouched on the outside, so that the still more wonderful deeds of the Mighty One would appear, and so that His name would be spoken of in all the earth.
So Zion was saved and Jerusalem delivered, and Israel was freed from tribulation.
All who were in the holy land rejoiced, and the name of the Mighty One was glorified, so that it was spoken of everywhere.
These are the bright waters you saw."

notes.text: "Hezekiah" (Hebrew *Chizqiyyahu*) means "Yahweh strengthens."
"Sennacherib" (Assyrian *Sin-ahhe-eriba*) means "Sin (the moon god) has replaced the brothers."

verses.text: "The black ninth waters you saw are all the wickedness in the days of Manasseh{a}, son of Hezekiah.

He did much that was ungodly. He killed the righteous, twisted judgment, shed the blood of the innocent, and violently defiled married women. He overturned the altars, destroyed their offerings, and drove out their priests so that they could not serve in the sanctuary.
He made an image with five faces. Four of them looked toward the four winds, and the fifth, on top of the image, stood as an opponent of the zeal of the Mighty One.
Then wrath went out from the presence of the Mighty One so that Zion would be uprooted, as also happened in your days.
A decree also went out against the two and a half tribes, that they too would be led away captive, as you have now seen.
Manasseh's ungodliness grew so great that it removed the praise of the Most High from the sanctuary.
For this reason Manasseh was called 'the ungodly' at that time, and in the end his dwelling was in the fire.
Though his prayer was heard by the Most High, in the end, when he was thrown into the bronze horse and the bronze horse melted, it served as a sign to him for the hour.
He had not lived perfectly, for he was not worthy. But from then on he would know by whom he would finally be tormented.
For the One who is able to help is also able to torment."

notes.text: "Manasseh" (Hebrew *Menashsheh*) means "he who makes forget."

verses.text: "So Manasseh acted ungodly and thought that in his time the Mighty One would not look into these things.
These are the black ninth waters you saw."
"The bright tenth waters you saw are the pure generations of Josiah{a}, king of Judah, who was the only one at that time who submitted to the Mighty One with all his heart and all his soul.

He cleansed the land of idols and made holy all the vessels that had been defiled. He restored the offerings to the altar and raised the horn of the holy ones. He lifted up the righteous and honored everyone wise in understanding. He brought the priests back to their service and destroyed and removed the magicians, enchanters, and necromancers from the land.
Not only did he put to death the ungodly who were alive, but they also took the bones of the dead out of the tombs and burned them with fire.

He set up the festivals and the Sabbaths in their holiness, and he burned their defiled ones in the fire. The lying prophets who deceived the people he also burned in the fire, and the people who had listened to them while they lived, he threw into the Kidron brook and heaped stones on them.

He was zealous with zeal for the Mighty One with all his soul, and he alone was firm in the law at that time, so that all the days of his life he left no uncircumcised person or anyone who practiced ungodliness in all the land.
So he will receive an eternal reward, and he will be glorified with the Mighty One above many at a later time.
For his sake and for the sake of those like him, the honorable glories of which you were told before were created and prepared. These are the bright waters you saw."

notes.text: "Josiah" (Hebrew *Yoshiyyahu*) probably means "Yahweh supports."

verses.text: "The black eleventh waters you saw are the calamity that is now falling on Zion.

Do you think there is no anguish among the angels in the presence of the Mighty One, that Zion was handed over like this, and that the nations boast in their hearts, gather before their idols, and say, 'She who so often trampled others is trampled down, and she who enslaved others has been enslaved'?
Do you think the Most High rejoices in these things, or that His name is glorified?
But how will it serve His righteous judgment?
After these things, those scattered among the nations will be seized by tribulation, and they will live in shame in every place.

For as long as Zion is handed over and Jerusalem laid waste, idols will prosper in the cities of the nations. The fragrant smoke of the incense of righteousness that comes by the law will be put out in Zion, and in every place in the region of Zion there will be the smoke of ungodliness.
But the king of Babylon, who has now destroyed Zion, will rise up and boast over the people, and he will say great things in his heart before the Most High.
But he too will fall in the end. These are the black waters."
"The bright twelfth waters you saw are this word.
After these things a time will come when your people fall into distress, so that they all run the risk of perishing together.
Even so, they will be saved, and their enemies will fall before them.
In due time they will have great joy.
At that time, after a short interval, Zion will be rebuilt again, its offerings will be restored, the priests will return to their service, and the nations will come to honor it.
Even so, it will not be fully as it was in the beginning.
But after these things there will be the fall of many nations.
These are the bright waters you saw."
"The last waters you saw, which were darker than all those before them, those that came after the twelfth and were gathered together, belong to the whole world.
The Most High made a division from the beginning, because He alone knows what will happen.
He foresaw six kinds of the outrages and ungodliness that would be done before Him.
And He foresaw six kinds of the good works of the righteous that would be done before Him, besides those that He Himself will do at the completion of the age.
For this reason there were no black waters mixed with black, and no bright with bright, for it is the end."
"Now hear the meaning of the last black waters that are to come after the black ones. This is the word.

See, the days are coming. When the time of the age has ripened and the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, the Mighty One will bring on the earth, its inhabitants, and its rulers a disturbance of spirit and a stupor of heart.
They will hate one another and stir one another up to fight. The lowly will rule over the honored, and those of low rank will be lifted above the famous.
The many will be handed over to the few, those who were nothing will rule over the strong, the poor will have more than the rich, and the ungodly will exalt themselves above the heroic.
The wise will be silent and the foolish will speak. Neither the thinking of people nor the counsel of the mighty will be confirmed then, and the hope of those who hope will not be confirmed.
When what was foretold has come to pass, confusion will fall on everyone. Some will fall in battle and some will perish in anguish,
and some will be destroyed by their own. Then the Most High will call up the nations He prepared beforehand, and they will come and make war on the leaders who are left at that time.
Whoever escapes the war will die in the earthquake, whoever escapes the earthquake will be burned by the fire, and whoever escapes the fire will be destroyed by famine.
Whoever, among the victors and the defeated, escapes all these things I have mentioned will be handed over to My servant, the Messiah.
For all the earth will devour its inhabitants."
"The holy land will have mercy on its own and protect its inhabitants at that time.
This is the vision you saw, and this is its meaning.
I have come to tell you these things because your prayer has been heard by the Most High."
"Now hear also about the bright lightning that is to come at the end, after these black waters. This is the word.

After the signs I told you of before have come, when the nations are in turmoil and the time of My Messiah has come, he will summon all the nations. Some of them he will spare, and some he will put to death.
These things will come on the nations that he spares.
Every nation that has not known Israel and has not trampled the seed of Jacob will indeed be spared.
This is because some from every nation will be made subject to your people.
But all who have ruled over you, or have known you, will be given up to the sword."
"When he has brought low everything in the world and has sat down in peace for the age on the throne of his kingdom, then joy will be revealed and rest will appear.
Then healing will come down like dew, and disease will withdraw. Worry, anguish, and lamentation will pass from among people, and gladness will spread through the whole earth.
No one will die before his time again, and no misfortune will strike suddenly.
Judgments, abusive talk, quarrels, revenge, bloodshed, passions, envy, hatred, and everything like these will go into condemnation when they are removed.
These are the very things that have filled this world with evils, and because of them human life has been greatly troubled.
Wild beasts will come out of the forest and serve people, and asps and dragons will come out of their holes to submit to a little child.
Women will no longer have pain when they give birth, and they will not suffer torment when they bring forth the fruit of the womb."
"In those days the reapers will not grow tired and the builders will not be worn out, for the work will move ahead quickly by itself, together with those who do it, in great peace.
For that time is the end of what is corruptible and the beginning of what is not corruptible.
So the things that were foretold will belong to it. It is far from evils and near to things that do not die.
This is the bright lightning that came after the last dark waters."
I answered, "Who can understand Your goodness, Lord? It cannot be grasped.
Who can search out Your compassion, which has no end?
Who can comprehend Your intelligence?
Who can recount the thoughts of Your mind?
Who among those who are born can hope to reach those things, unless it is someone to whom You are merciful and gracious?
If You did not have compassion on humanity, those under Your right hand could not reach those things, but only those counted by name can be called.
