But if we who exist know why we have come, and submit to the One who brought us out of Egypt, we will come again and remember the things that have passed, and we will rejoice over what has been.

But if we do not know why we have come, and do not acknowledge the rule of the One who brought us up out of Egypt, we will come again and look for the things of the present, and be grieved with pain over what has happened."

chapters.heading: Baruch's hymn

verses.text: He answered me, "Since the meaning of this vision has been explained to you as you asked, hear the word of the Most High, so that you may know what will happen to you after these things.
You will surely depart from this earth, but not to death. You will be kept until the end of the times.

So go up to the top of that mountain, and all the regions of that land will pass before you, together with the shape of the inhabited world, the tops of the mountains, the depths of the valleys, the depths of the seas, and the number of the rivers, so that you may see what you are leaving and where you are going.

This will happen after forty days. So go now, and during these days teach the people as far as you can, so that they may learn and not die at the last time, but may learn so that they live in the last times."

chapters.heading: Baruch is told to teach the people for forty days

verses.text: I, Baruch, went there and came to the people. I gathered them together, from the greatest to the least, and said to them,
"Listen, children of Israel. See how many of you remain from the twelve tribes of Israel.
To you and to your fathers the Lord gave a law more excellent than any given to all other peoples.
Because your brothers broke the commands of the Most High, He did not spare the earlier ones, and He gave the later ones also into captivity. He did not leave a remnant of them,
but see, you are here with me.
If you direct your ways rightly, you also will not depart as your brothers departed, but they will come to you.
The One you worship is merciful, the One in whom you hope is gracious, and He is true, so that He will do good and not evil.
Have you not seen here what has happened to Zion?
Or do you perhaps think the place had sinned and was overthrown for that reason? Or that the land had acted foolishly and so was handed over?
Do you not know that because of you who sinned, what did not sin was overthrown, and because of those who did wickedly, what did not act foolishly was handed over to its enemies?"
The whole people answered me, "As far as we can recall the good things the Mighty One has done for us, we recall them, and the things we do not remember He knows in His mercy.
Even so, do this for us, your people: write also to our brothers in Babylon a letter of teaching and a scroll of hope, so that you may strengthen them too before you leave us.
The shepherds of Israel have perished, the lamps that gave light have gone out, and the fountains have held back the streams we used to drink from.
We are left in the darkness, among the trees of the forest, and in the thirst of the wilderness."
I answered them, "Shepherds, lamps, and fountains come from the law. Though we depart, the law remains.
If you therefore respect the law and give yourselves to wisdom, a lamp will not be missing, a shepherd will not fail, and a fountain will not dry up.
Even so, as you have asked me, I will write to your brothers in Babylon and send it by men. In the same way I will write to the nine and a half tribes and send it by a bird."
On the twenty-first day of the eighth month ({a}October–November), I, Baruch, came and sat down under the oak, in the shade of its branches. No one was with me, and I was alone.
I wrote these two letters. One I sent by an eagle to the nine and a half tribes, and the other I sent to those in Babylon by three men.
I called the eagle and said these words to it:
"The Most High made you higher than all birds.

Now go, and do not linger anywhere, do not enter a nest, and do not settle on any tree until you have crossed the breadth of the many waters of the river Euphrates{b} and have gone to the people who live there, and drop this letter to them.
Remember that at the time of the flood Noah{c} received an olive branch from a dove when he sent it out from the ark.
The ravens also served Elijah{d}, bringing him food, as they had been commanded.
Solomon, too, in the time of his kingdom, whenever he wished to send or look for anything, commanded a bird to go, and it obeyed him as he commanded.
Now do not let this tire you. Turn neither right nor left, but fly straight, so that you keep the command of the Mighty One, as I have told you."

notes.text: October–November: The text says the "eighth month" of the Hebrew calendar, which is Marcheshvan.
"Euphrates" (Hebrew *Perat*) is the great river of Mesopotamia, whose name means "fruitful."
"Noah" (Hebrew *Noach*) is linked in Genesis 5 with "rest" or "comfort."
"Elijah" (Hebrew *Eliyyahu*) means "my God is Yahweh."

chapters.heading: Baruch's address, and his two letters

verses.text: These are the words of the letter that Baruch, son of Neriah, sent to the nine and a half tribes across the river Euphrates, in which these things were written.

Baruch, son of Neriah, says this to the brothers carried into captivity: "Mercy and peace." My brothers, I keep in mind the love of the One who created us. He loved us from of old and never hated us, but above all He trained us.
I know that all of us, the twelve tribes, are bound by one bond, since we were born from one father.

So I have been all the more careful to leave you the words of this letter before I die, so that you may be comforted about the evils that have come on you, and may also grieve over the evil that has come on your brothers. I also want you to justify His judgment,

which He decreed against you, that you be carried away captive, since what you have suffered is out of proportion to what you have done, so that in the last times you may be found worthy of your fathers.

So if you consider that you have suffered these things for your good, so that in the end you will not be condemned and tormented, then you will receive eternal hope. Above all, you must destroy from your heart the empty error that caused you to leave this place.

If you do this, He will always remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those more excellent than we are that He will never forget or abandon us, but will gather again, with great mercy, those who were scattered.

chapters.heading: The letter to the nine and a half tribes

verses.text: Now, my brothers, first learn what happened to Zion: how Nebuchadnezzar{a}, king of Babylon, came up against us.
We sinned against the One who made us and did not keep the commandments He gave us, yet He has not punished us as we deserved.
What happened to you we also suffer in a still greater degree, for it happened to us as well.

notes.text: "Nebuchadnezzar" (Babylonian *Nabu-kudurri-usur*) means "Nabu, protect my heir."

verses.text: Now, my brothers, I tell you that when the enemy had surrounded the city, the angels of the Most High were sent, and they overthrew the fortifications of the strong wall and destroyed the firm iron corners, which could not be uprooted.
Even so, they hid all the vessels of the sanctuary, so that the enemy could not take possession of them.

When they had done this, they handed over to the enemy the overthrown wall, the plundered house, the burned temple, and the people, who were overcome because they had been given up, so that the enemy could not boast and say, "By force we have been able to lay waste even the house of the Most High in war."
They have also bound your brothers and led them away to Babylon, and made them live there.
But we have been left here, very few.
This is the tribulation I wrote to you about.
I know that the comfort of the inhabitants of Zion consoles you, since, as long as you knew it was prospering, your comfort was greater than the tribulation you endured in having to leave it.
Now hear the word about comfort.
I was mourning over Zion, and I asked the Most High for mercy, and I said,
"How long will these things last for us? Will these evils come on us always?"

The Mighty One acted according to the abundance of His mercies, and the Most High according to the greatness of His compassion. He revealed the word to me so that I would receive comfort. He showed me visions so that I would not endure anguish again, and He made known to me the mystery of the times and showed me the coming of the hours.
So, my brothers, I have written to you so that you may comfort yourselves in the abundance of your tribulations.

Know that our Maker will surely avenge us on all our enemies for everything they have done to us. The end that the Most High will bring is very near, and His mercy that is coming and the end of His judgment are not far off at all.
We now see the abundance of the nations' prosperity, though they act ungodly, but they will be like a vapor.
We see the greatness of their power, though they do wickedly, but they will be made like a drop of water.
We see the firmness of their strength, though they resist the Mighty One every hour, but they will be counted as spit.
We consider the glory of their greatness, though they do not keep the statutes of the Most High, but they will pass away like smoke.
We think about the beauty of their grace, though they deal in pollution, but they will fade away like grass that withers.
We consider the strength of their cruelty, though they do not remember its end, but they will be broken like a wave that passes.
We take note of the boasting of their might, though they deny the kindness of God who gave it to them, but they will pass away like a passing cloud.
For the Most High will surely hasten His times, and He will surely bring on His hours.
He will surely judge those who are in His world, and He will visit all things in truth through all their hidden works.
He will surely examine the secret thoughts and everything stored in the inner rooms of all the members of the human body, and He will make it plain before everyone with rebuke.
So let none of these present things rise into your hearts, but above all let us wait expectantly, because what has been promised to us will come.
Let us not now look to the pleasures of the nations in the present, but let us remember what has been promised to us in the end.
For the ends of the times and seasons, and whatever goes with them, will surely pass by together.
The end of the age will then show the great power of its ruler, when all things come to judgment.
So prepare your hearts for what you believed before, so that you do not end up in bondage in both worlds, led away captive here and tormented there.
For in everything that exists now, or has passed, or is to come, neither is the evil fully evil, nor again the good fully good.
All the health of this time is turning into sickness,
all the might of this time is turning into weakness, and all the force of this time is turning into helplessness.
Every energy of youth is turning into old age and decline, and every graceful beauty of this time is turning faded and hateful.
Every proud rule of the present is turning into humiliation and shame,
every praise of the glory of this time is turning into the shame of silence, and every empty splendor and insolence of this time is turning into voiceless ruin.
Every delight and joy of this time is turning to worms and corruption,
every clamor of the pride of this time is turning into dust and stillness.
Every possession of riches in this time is being turned into Sheol alone,
all the plunder of passion in this time is turning into unwilling death, and every passion of the desires of this time is turning into a judgment of torment.
Every scheme and trick of this time is turning into a proof of the truth,
every sweetness of perfumes in this time is turning into judgment and condemnation,
and every love of lying is turning into disgrace through the truth.
Since all these things are done now, does anyone think they will not be avenged? But the end of all things will come to the truth.

See, I have made these things known to you while I am alive. I said it so that you would learn what is excellent, for the Mighty One has commanded me to teach you, and I will set before you some of the commands of His judgment before I die.
Remember that Moses once called heaven and earth to witness against you and said, "If you break the law you will be scattered, but if you keep it you will be kept."
He also told you other things when you, the twelve tribes, were together in the desert.
After his death you threw them away from you, and for this reason what had been foretold came on you.
Moses told you before these things happened to you, and now they have happened to you, for you abandoned the law.
I also say to you, now that you have suffered, that if you obey what has been said to you, you will receive from the Mighty One whatever has been stored up and kept for you.
Let this letter be a testimony between me and you, so that you remember the commands of the Mighty One, and so that I also have a defense before the One who sent me.
Remember the law and Zion, the holy land and your brothers, and the covenant of your fathers, and do not forget the festivals and the Sabbaths.
Hand on this letter and the traditions of the law to your sons after you, as your fathers handed them on to you.

At all times ask persistently and pray earnestly with your whole heart that the Mighty One may be reconciled to you, and that He may not count the multitude of your sins but remember the uprightness of your fathers.
For if He does not judge us according to the abundance of His mercies, woe to all of us who are born."
"Know also that in former times, in the generations of old, our fathers had helpers, righteous men and holy prophets.
We were in our own land, and they helped us when we sinned. They interceded for us with the One who made us, because they trusted in their works, and the Mighty One heard their prayer and forgave us.

But now the righteous have been gathered, the prophets have fallen asleep, and we too have gone out from the land. Zion has been taken from us, and now we have nothing except the Mighty One and His law.
So if we direct and set our hearts in order, we will receive everything we lost, and far better things many times over.
What we lost was subject to corruption, and what we will receive will not be corruptible.
I have also written like this to our brothers in Babylon, so that I may bear witness to them as well about these very things.
Let all the things I have mentioned be always before your eyes, because we are still in the spirit and power of our freedom.
Again, the Most High is patient with us here. He has shown us what is to come and has not hidden from us what will happen in the end.

So before judgment claims what is its own and truth what is due to it, let us prepare our souls so that we possess and are not possessed, so that we hope and are not put to shame, and so that we rest with our fathers and are not tormented with our enemies.

For the youth of the world is past, the strength of creation is already spent, and the coming of the times is very near. Indeed, they have gone by. The pitcher is near the cistern, the ship near the port, the course of the journey near the city, and life near its end.
Prepare your souls again, so that when you sail and step off the ship, you may have rest

and not be condemned when you depart. For when the Most High brings all these things to pass, there will be no more a place for repentance, no limit to the times, no duration for the hours, no change of ways, no place for prayer, no sending of petitions, no receiving of knowledge, no giving of love, no place of repentance for the soul, no pleading for offenses, no intercession of the fathers, no prayer of the prophets, and no help of the righteous.
There is the sentence of corruption, the way of fire, and the path that leads to Gehenna.
For this reason there is one law through one, one age, and an end for all who are in it.
Then He will keep safe those He can forgive and at the same time destroy those who are stained with sins."
When you receive this letter of mine, read it carefully in your congregations.
Think it over, above all on the days of your fasts.
Remember me by means of this letter, as I also remember you in it, always. Farewell.
When I had finished all the words of this letter and had written it carefully to its close, I folded it, sealed it securely, tied it to the neck of the eagle, and let it go and sent it off.
